spec.requirement: `auger spec validate` and `auger spec check` read one corpus through one loader: every `*.xml` file below the spec root is indexed, each document's root element is `<spec>` in the `urn:auger:spec:1` namespace carrying `schema-version="1.0"`, `id` and `version`, and a document declaring a DOCTYPE or ENTITY is refused (`external-entity-forbidden`). Because both verbs hand the same documents to the same obligation pass, one corpus earns one verdict and one diagnostic, and a document the published XSD rejects is refused (`schema-invalid`) even where the code's own rules would have accepted it.
spec.verification: Drives `spec validate` and `spec check` as subprocesses over every fixture corpus root and asserts the same exit code, the same diagnostic (byte-identical stderr on refusal) and the same verdict on acceptance.

A well-formed document whose only defect is an attribute the grammar does not declare is refused by both verbs with `schema-invalid`, naming the document and the attribute — the backstop the code's own rules leave open.
